newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Banks watch Ka Wah progress.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Banks watch Ka Wah progress.

text.p: Banks are watching Ka Wah Bank Ltd's 135 million mark floating-rate note to see if it inspires other second-tier banks in Hong Kong to try their luck in the Euro markets.
They said they would also be watching the swap back into U.S. or H.K. dollars to see how much it cut funding costs.
The deal has already been criticised as too low-yielding for a first-time visitor to the Euro market, some bankers said.

Some said they thought Ka Wah Bank, majority-owned by China International Trust and Investment Corp, was seeking to build European relationships with the five-year FRN, issued at 50 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).
The Philippines is watching U.S. interest rates before deciding on whether to issue its US$1.25 billion Yankee bond, a Philippine official said on Thursday.
Central bank governor Gabriel Singson said the Philippines was ready to move quickly, if necessary, having completed registration and roadshows.
He said Manila was keeping a close eye on U.S. interest rates; the U.S. long bond had been between 6.50 and 6.60 percent in January when it decided on a Yankee bond.
The Philippines' bond issuance plans were boosted earlier this week after Moody's Investors Service upgraded Manila's foreign currency debt ratings to Ba2 from Ba3.
A co-arranger group is being formed for Taiwan chipmaker Mosel Vitelic Inc, which is raising US$100 million through a five-year floating-rate note issue in Hong Kong, bankers said on Thursday.
The FRN will be launched through a special-purpose vehicle called Vision 2000 Ventures Cayman Island, and the deal is guaranteed by Mosel Vitelic.
Issued at par to float at 47.5 basis points over LIBOR, the FRN includes a three year put and call option.
Mosel Vitelic also plans to issue about 12 billion to 15 billion yen in Samurai bonds in mid-June, according to Nikko Securities Co, which is underwriting the deal.
While Taiwanese firms have raised funds in the Euro market, it will be the first time a Taiwan private firm has offered yen-denominated bonds publicly, Nikko Securities said.
Fellow Taiwanese Chungtex Electronic Co has priced its US$25 million three-year FRN at 70 basis points over LIBOR.
The deal includes annual put options.
Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd closed its HK$800 million staff housing mortgages securitisation, arranger Societe Generale said.
Household product-maker Magician Industries (Holdings) Ltd signed its HK$150 million term loan facility to fund expansion in China and overseas markets.
